messages.text: Tuesday, November 17 · Canton, Michigan
Polish fortune-telling and the Leonids arrive under overcast skies

The day brings a quiet, gray chill to Canton as the Leonid meteor shower reaches its peak activity. Local residents can find warmth in traditional cultural gatherings nearby while the sky remains obscured.
Expect an overcast day with a high near 55 degrees and a low around 30 degrees.
The sun rises at 7:27 AM and sets at 5:10 PM, with the moon in its first-quarter phase at 47.8 percent illumination.
A moment for tradition
Visit Haven Hall in Ann Arbor at 11:00 AM for the Andrzejki celebration to explore Polish fortune-telling, music, and traditional games.
Members should prepare for the 862 Meeting scheduled for tomorrow, November 18, at 6:30 PM.
Crisis response and campus oversight

Ann Arbor has officially launched A2 REACH, a new crisis response team pairing police officers with social workers to assist those in mental health distress. Meanwhile, the University of Michigan Faculty Senate recently issued a vote of no confidence regarding police and labor negotiations.
Looking toward the week
Keep the Girls Gear Up outreach event on your radar for this Friday, November 21, at 7:30 AM.

Wednesday, November 18 · Canton, Michigan
Bronze bells, ancient ice, and a quiet shift toward winter

The day brings overcast skies and mild temperatures as we settle into the late autumn rhythm. Local focus turns to the resonance of historical instruments and the long-range implications of distant planetary science.
Expect overcast conditions today with a high near 57 degrees and a low around 27 degrees.
The sun rises at 7:28 AM and sets at 5:09 PM, with the moon in its first-quarter phase at 57.6 percent illumination.
Midday music and afternoon inquiry
Tiffany Ng performs a carillon recital on the 53 bronze bells of Burton Memorial Tower at 12:00 PM. Later, the East Hall hosts a seminar on algebraic combinatorics at 2:30 PM.
The 862 Meeting is scheduled for this evening at 6:30 PM.
Faculty senate and local governance

The University of Michigan Faculty Senate recently passed a vote of no confidence regarding university leadership and police department negotiations. This follows broader regional shifts in political control that continue to influence policy discussions across the state.
Looking toward the weekend
The Girls Gear Up outreach event is set for the morning of November 21 at 7:30 AM.
